From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fintegrate.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T12:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next steps (reranker integration)

Alex — great questions, answered inline below. Looping in Rishi (solutions) and Dylan (ML infra) to take the deep technical dive. They'll lead on the evaluation plan and SDK examples.

1) Reranker API shape
- Redwood's ranking endpoint returns a list of results with score and an optional structured_output field when you enable structured output/tool-calling on the model. Structured output is arbitrary JSON (we enforce a schema if you provide one) — good for extracted entities or downstream metadata.
- Example response fields: id, score, snippet, structured_output.

2) Top_k tuning guidance
- Start: candidate pool of 100 is a good default for document corpora ~1M. Sweep: 50 / 100 / 200.
- Tradeoffs: larger candidate pools increase recall but add latency on the rerank stage (linear in candidate count for cross-encoder rerankers). For our cross-encoder family you can expect ~3–6ms per candidate on a p3-like SKU; with batching/optimizations we often keep p95 for the rerank stage under 200–300ms for 100 candidates.

3) Embeddings pipeline
- Options: (A) Push embeddings into your existing ANN (OpenSearch) and call Redwood only at query time for the reranker; or (B) store embeddings with Redwood (we can ingest via API) and let our candidate selector handle retrieval.
- For PoC we recommend you keep your ANN and call Redwood at query time — lower lift. If you want unified monitoring/cost visibility we can ingest embeddings into your dedicated Redwood workspace.

4) Auth & routing
- PoC: API key + per-route quotas.
- Production Private: support for SAML SSO, OIDC, and AWS IAM role mapping for Private on AWS (VPC routing + peering where needed).
- Networking: for Private deployments we provide a customer-managed VPC connector and explicit egress rules; we'll share a short network diagram in the deep-dive.

5) Eval metrics & tooling
- We'll compute: NDCG@5/10, MRR, Precision@1/3/5, Recall@k, and latency percentiles for the rerank stage (p50/p95/p99).
- Tooling: we run evaluation harnesses in Python (pytest-style runner) and can share a Jupyter notebook that computes these. We can also produce a short report (CSV + plots).

Next steps: Thu 2026-05-21 10:00am PT works for us — Rishi and Dylan will send the calendar invite and a short agenda. Please drop a sanitized CSV (query,id, relevance) in the shared doc link and we'll prep the initial run.

Attachments referenced: redwood-reranker-arch.pdf (attached), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (attached).

Thanks,
Marissa

Alex / Priya — I'll lead the technical deep-dive. A few quick notes to prep so we can use the time efficiently: 

- Bring a sample CSV (query_id, query_text, doc_id, relevance_label). If you can include candidate lists (ANN hits) that's ideal; if not we'll generate candidates from your text store.

- Quick architecture options (we'll demo both during the call):
  * Two-stage (recommended PoC): ANN retrieval in your infra -> call Redwood /v1/ranking to rerank top_k candidates.
  * Unified: ingest embeddings into Redwood + use our retrieval service -> rerank (lower network hops, easier monitoring).

- API & SDK notes (short examples):
  * Curl (rerank):
    curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/ranking" \n      -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n      -d '{"query_embedding": [...], "candidate_embeddings": [[...]], "candidate_ids": ["doc1","doc2"], "top_k": 100, "model": "rerank-cross-1"}'

  * Python (SDK pseudo):
    from redwood import Client
    client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    resp = client.ranking.rerank(query_embedding=query_emb, candidates=candidate_list, top_k=100, model="rerank-cross-1")
    # resp.results -> list of {id, score, snippet, structured_output}

- Structured output: enable schema enforcement at request-time if you want predictable JSON (we'll validate and return model outputs under that schema).
- Evaluation plan (we'll run these during the PoC): sweep top_k in [50,100,200], compare bi-encoder+dot-product reordering vs cross-encoder rerank, compute NDCG@10/MRR/Precision@3, and report latency distribution for rerank stage.

If you can upload the CSV to the Google Doc link before Wed EOD we'll pre-run 1–2 configs and have results to discuss. Sending the calendar invite now.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
